blocks.text:
**Evidence labels matter.** A source-defined event has an emitter in the versioned implementation. A declared desktop analytics type has a literal declaration in the shipped bundle, but may be a nested payload type, a gated feature, or unused compatibility code. A documented cloud record has a public export contract. None of those, by itself, proves that an individual event was emitted by your account or reached a collector.

The catalogs deliberately retain experimental and compatibility entries. A name is not labeled deprecated merely because it is absent from one document, disabled locally, or unfamiliar. Dynamic names, runtime extensions, and proprietary server-only instrumentation cannot be exhaustively recovered from public documentation or a desktop binary. Those boundaries are stated rather than filled with invented names.

rows: CLI embedded in that desktop bundle
Desktop and terminal version strings differ
Shared Rust files in the downloaded trees were compared; no differing shared `.rs` files were found
Current server export schema, independently versioned from desktop and CLI
A desktop build number does not pin their backend implementation

The installed versions above are verified. “Newest” is time- and rollout-dependent; this document pins the requested builds, rather than treating a version string as proof of every account's update channel.

Sources: [CLI 0.163.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.163.0), [desktop runtime source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2), [public Admin API reference](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference), and the installed bundle metadata.

sections.title: The important answers before the catalogs

blocks.text:
1. **The four surfaces do not have one interchangeable telemetry schema.** `codex.tool_result`, a desktop structured analytics message, a `CODEX_LOG` record and a daily usage row describe different layers.
2. **OTel logging is richer than the default trace-event path.** Detailed logs can include account email, tool arguments and output. The trace-safe event path omits selected sensitive fields, but is not a guarantee that every span or arbitrary custom attribute is content-free.
3. **`otel.log_user_prompt = false` is not a universal content-redaction switch.** It redacts the prompt field on the prompt event. Tool arguments/output, explicitly enabled final-answer logs, assessment rationale, feedback and compliance content have separate behavior.
4. **Version 0.163.0 contradicts part of the current public configuration prose:** `analytics.enabled = false` disables the built-in Statsig metrics route, but does **not** disable an explicitly configured custom OTLP metrics exporter. Disable that route with `otel.metrics_exporter = "none"`. The versioned implementation is authoritative for this manual.
5. **New cloud orchestration does not stream into the old local collector.** Supported local execution records can still arrive locally. Supported cloud records come from Compliance APIs. Repointing the local collector does not restore the missing cloud orchestration stream.
6. **The supplied singular cloud URL is the legacy guide.** New reusable cloud setups use the plural `cloud-environments` guide. Legacy workflows still include Code Review and GitHub/Linear integrations; the docs state an intention to deprecate that experience, not that every legacy workflow is already gone.

Sources: [0.163.0 exporter selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs), [log/trace filters](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/provider.rs), [cloud/local coverage](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-local-access#review-opentelemetry-and-audit-coverage), [new cloud](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments), [legacy cloud](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment).

sections.title: What telemetry does on your Mac

blocks.text:
Telemetry observes operations; it is not itself a grant of permission to edit files, control apps, record the screen, or operate a browser. Those capabilities belong to the underlying tools and their permissions. Telemetry can record that an operation was requested, decided, started, completed, failed, or timed out. Those states are not interchangeable.

Runtime instrumentation allocates counters and buffers, records timestamps and attributes, serializes batches and makes outbound collector requests when configured. Local diagnostic logging can write to Codex's bounded stores; an explicitly configured `log_dir` also enables the plaintext TUI log. A larger tool-output logging limit increases potential payload size and disclosure. Export failure is not proof that the underlying operation failed, and successful operation is not proof that export succeeded.

Native desktop product analytics is separate. The shipped app includes structured event transport, Statsig experiment/exposure handling, error reporting and native diagnostic logging. Static inclusion is not proof that every route is active in your account. This manual contains identifiers and schemas, not your private event values, credentials, conversation contents or captured network traffic.

Cloud-only work records activity on the cloud side. When a cloud task uses a local executor, that executor can generate local records too. A cloud `EXECUTION_REQUESTED` event means a launch was requested; an executor `process_exit` record supplies a different observation about the process outcome.

No telemetry settings were changed to prepare this document. The inspection used version output, installed static assets, versioned source and public schemas; it did not run test model tasks or turn on content export.

The table describes the 0.163.0 runtime configuration model. Put telemetry routing in the user-level configuration or an applicable managed layer. Project-local telemetry routing is restricted. Exporter configuration and the consuming process's effective configuration must agree; a file edit alone does not prove a running daemon reloaded it.

blocks.text:
Here `<exporter>` means `exporter`, `trace_exporter` or `metrics_exporter`; `<transport>` means `otlp-http` or `otlp-grpc`. The configuration types share exporter structures, but Statsig is intended for metrics. These are configuration keys, not emitted attributes.

An explicit all-three-runtime-exporters-off fragment is:

```toml
[analytics]
enabled = false

[otel]
exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
log_user_prompt = false
log_agent_responses = false
log_guardian_assessments = false
```

This fragment is illustrative, not applied. It is not a promise to turn off every hosted audit record, service operational log, desktop crash route or browser-site analytic. Those have distinct owners and policies.

Sources: [configuration types](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/config/src/types.rs), [configuration defaults](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/config/otel.rs), [exporter selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs), [tool preview limit](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs), [local diagnostics](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/environment-variables).

blocks.text:
The common-field list applies to emitters using the shared macros. It is not a universal required-field schema for every named diagnostic or executor event. Optional values can be absent. Global/process metrics do not all pass through the same session wrapper.

Durations ending `_ms` are milliseconds; executor metrics ending `_seconds` use seconds. `codex.goal.duration_s` uses seconds. `codex.turn.cost_microusd` accumulates millionths of USD. Some detailed event durations are formatted as strings by the tracing emitter. Preserve actual wire types rather than assuming every duration is a numeric attribute. A histogram of tool-call counts is not a counter, even when its name contains `call`.

Sources: [shared event macros](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/events/shared.rs), [metric tags](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/tags.rs), [metric resource construction](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/client.rs).

`codex.tool_result` detailed logs contain raw arguments and a bounded output preview. `output_truncated` says that the telemetry preview was shortened; it does not certify that the original tool output was complete. `tool_result_seq` orders result recording across the process, not tool starts, and resets when the process restarts. The trace-safe counterpart records lengths, line count and origin instead of arguments/output content.

`codex.agent_response` is separately opted in, logs only eligible live final-answer items, deduplicates within a turn, and caps exported text at 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. It skips internal/review/compaction/memory-consolidation sessions. Exported memory citations are stripped from the copy; stored conversation history is not rewritten.

`codex.guardian_assessment` is separately opted in. It records terminal review status and, when available, outcome, risk and authorization classification. Failure/timeout/cancellation need not have a model outcome. The rationale cap is 65,536 bytes. A fail-closed denial is not evidence that a model classified the action as denied.

`codex.skill_invocation` records detected use and scope, not successful task completion. It omits skill contents and resource paths. Authentication storage metrics use bounded classifications rather than passwords or tokens. Authentication diagnostics can indicate that an environment variable/header is present without including its secret value.

On `codex.sse_event`, the historical field `tool_token_count` is assigned from `usage.total_tokens`. It therefore means total token usage in this emitter, despite the misleading name; it must not be added again as a separate tool-token category.

The new cloud/local join is explicit: cloud `CODEX_LOG / EXECUTION_REQUESTED` contains `launch_trace_id` and `launch_span_id`; local executor lifecycle logs retain them as `launch.trace_id` and `launch.span_id`. Keep the associated workspace/thread/tool identifiers too. Do not join unrelated products merely because they have fields named `session_id` or `conversation.id`.

Sources: [tool-result emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/tool_result.rs), [answer emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/agent_response.rs), [assessment emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/guardian_assessment.rs), [executor lifecycle](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/exec-server/src/process_telemetry.rs), [Codex compliance contract](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference).

### How the runtime carries trace context

The runtime can read `TRACEPARENT` and optional `TRACESTATE` from its environment. The environment-derived context is initialized once per process. Invalid incoming context is ignored; it does not fall back to an unrelated active span. For supported outgoing HTTP paths, the supplied span’s valid context replaces existing `traceparent`/`tracestate` headers. Configured `otel.tracestate` entries are merged into that context. These mechanisms carry correlation; they do not grant authorization or prove that the receiving service exported a span. [Implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/trace_context.rs).

sections.title: Native product analytics in the CLI/runtime

blocks.text:
This is a separate serialized-event client, with a destination formed as `<base_url>/codex/analytics-events/events`. It is not the configured OTel log endpoint. Eligibility and authentication are handled by the analytics client; some plugin-related records have explicit API-key support. The debug-only `CODEX_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_CAPTURE_FILE` can redirect these payloads to a local capture file in debug builds; it is not a supported release-build switch for capturing everything.

The request envelope contains an `events` array. The event records below use native `event_type` strings; payload layouts are described in the following source-struct catalog. A family name may be reused for started/completed or other lifecycle stages.

**Compatibility detail:** `codex_accepted_line_fingerprints` retains the `line_fingerprints` field, but the pinned schema makes it an empty array. The implementation no longer generates line fingerprints. The nested historical marker `codex.accepted_line_fingerprints` is retained separately; it is not an additional current top-level OTel event. [Source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/analytics/src/events.rs).

### Analytics payload structures

The following structures are reachable through the serialized `TrackEventsRequest` envelope. In-process queue, reducer and bookkeeping structs are excluded because they are not payload schemas. These are implementation schemas, not a promise of a public ingestion API. `Option<T>` is optional at the source level; exact omission/null behavior also depends on serialization annotations. `Vec<T>` is a list. Flattened fields should be expanded by the serializer, not treated as a mandatory nested object.

The installed Electron bundle contains a separate structured analytics implementation. It can form a Statsig or Segment-style envelope, with an event ID, event creation time, event type, event parameters and an `@type` marker. The marker is formed from `openai.buf.dev/openai/protobuf-analytics-events/` plus the declared protobuf analytics type. Client metadata, device/user/account context and transport choice depend on the path. These are internal schemas, not a supported user-selectable OTel collector interface.

The bundle also includes Statsig exposure identifiers (`statsig::gate_exposure`, `statsig::config_exposure`, `statsig::layer_exposure`), diagnostic/error integrations and native telemetry-user updates. A library or identifier being bundled does not prove the feature is enabled or that data was transmitted. No claims about your actual historical activity are made here.

### Desktop structured-event envelope

The installed bundle has two builders. Both place event-specific fields inside `eventParams`; the Segment-style builder explicitly adds more identity/context fields. The Statsig builder’s smaller local envelope does not establish that the SDK adds no identity metadata later.

### Desktop payload fields found at call sites

This expands the declaration catalog with statically visible payloads. The analysis resolved local bindings and named imports/exports across 347 bundle modules. It found 1722 calls referencing 1015 declared type descriptors, with 4014 distinct type/field pairs. A reference is evidence that code passes that descriptor and payload to a function; it is not proof that the function ran or that a service accepted the event.

Field paths are the union of visible object properties at those references, including resolvable object initializers and inline payload callbacks. Dots below express nested object paths. They are not invented dotted JSON keys. These are not required-field schemas. Object spreads, computed keys, helper calls, function arguments, mutations and account-dependent branches can add, remove or transform fields. Dynamic payloads are marked; absence from a static payload is not proof that a runtime field never exists.

The value column preserves literal values and uppercase enum members visible in expressions. It is a subset observed in code, not the complete allowed-value domain. A runtime expression means the value is supplied or computed; it does not mean the value is always present. S-number references are local to each type. Their offsets use JavaScript UTF-16 indexing in the extracted bundle file, whereas declaration offsets above use Unicode character indexing. No private runtime values were captured.

Common correlation fields such as `conversationId`, `threadId`, `turnId`, `messageId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, `organizationId`, `userId` and `requestId` retain the identity domain stated by their names. `action`, `surface`, `source`, `stage`, `result`, `outcome`, `reason` and `status` are event-specific classifications; their domains must not be merged merely because the keys match. Fields ending in `Ms` name milliseconds; other timing units must be checked at their source. Counts, flags, content fields and identifiers are not interchangeable.

sections.title: chatgpt.com and new Codex Cloud: public export contracts

blocks.text:
These services expose workspace records and aggregated analytics. They do not promise that every local `codex.*` event has a corresponding cloud record. The desktop’s embedded web assets are also not proof of the exact JavaScript or server experiment active on chatgpt.com at another time.

The new cloud environment guide is [Cloud environments](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments). The supplied [singular cloud-environment URL](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment) documents **Codex Cloud (Legacy)**. Creating a new cloud environment, publishing a snapshot, and continuing an existing task have different lifecycle effects; do not assume one environment event covers every snapshot/task transition.

For cloud orchestration with local computer access, collect supported local execution OTel and supported cloud Compliance records separately. The new cloud record `EXECUTION_REQUESTED` supplies the launch trace/span pair for joining to executor events. This is best-effort correlation; it does not establish successful execution. [Cloud/local audit coverage](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-local-access#review-opentelemetry-and-audit-coverage).

### Public log families

The family selector on a file-list request is named `event_type`. Inside a JSONL record, the outer `type` identifies its family; families such as `CODEX_LOG` also contain an inner `event_type` for the action. These levels must not be flattened into one ambiguous field.

rows: `payload` with turn, model, usage, skill/plugin and artifact attribution
Presentation-style schema with Word client identity
Hourly paid-plan usage and billing measures

blocks.text:
Source for the cloud record/schema tables in this chapter: [OpenAI public Admin API reference, OpenAPI 2.5.39](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference).

### Shared compliance envelope

rows: Event/action time in UTC; not necessarily ingestion time
Actor variant; affects the available identity fields
Redacted API-key identity for API-key actors
System actor identifier where the family uses a system actor

blocks.text:
The file API is at-least-once: deduplicate by `event_id`. Files are immutable; event updates can therefore produce additional records. Freshness reports the maximum retained event time, not a guarantee that every earlier event has arrived. The general file retention window is 30 days; specialized materialized data has different latency. `CODEX_TURN` is generated approximately two hours after its source hour; `COSTS` expects roughly three to five hours.

### CODEX_LOG: every documented sub-event

Every `event_details` variant has `detail_type`. Optional fields and availability vary with the emitting client.

Plugin key family: `plugin_id`, `plugin_release_id`, `plugin_version`, `plugin_name`, `plugin_display_name`, `marketplace_name`, `plugin_scope`, `plugin_creator_account_user_id`. Scope values are `GLOBAL`, `WORKSPACE`, `USER`. Response `token_usage` contains `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`.

Cloud decision values: `approved`, `approved_with_amendment`, `approved_for_session`, `approved_mcp_policy_amendment`, `approved_with_network_policy_allow`, `denied_with_network_policy_deny`, `denied`, `timed_out`, `abort`. Decision source can be `automated_reviewer`, `config`, or `user`. These decisions do not contain prompt, tool-argument or output content. Tool-call IDs differ from inference request IDs.

`agent` contains `type`, optional verified deployment `id`, and optional `name`; legacy `agent_id` and `agent_name` remain compatibility fields. Do not merge agent identity and human actor identity.

### CONVERSATION_MESSAGE: field inventory

rows: Applied raw custom instructions when available
Snapshot flag; missing historical value means unknown, not false

blocks.text:
User client types: `unknown`, `desktop_web`, `ios_web`, `ios_app`, `macos_app`, `windows_app`, `android_web`, `android_app`, `chatgpt_api`. Group by conversation, order using message relationships, and retain updates sharing a message ID rather than confusing message identity with event identity.

### CODEX_TURN: materialized turn payload

Fields under `payload`: `hour_partition`, `turn_id`, `turn_key`, `thread_id`, `session_id`, `product_client_id`, `model`, `reasoning_effort`, `speed`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `duration_ms`, `response_count`, `classification`, `credits`, `cost_usd`, `estimated_cost_usd`, `tags`, `token_usage`, `skills`, `plugins`, `artifact_actions`.

rows: Contains `automation` for an automation-initiated turn; otherwise empty

blocks.text:
This is an hourly materialized view, not the raw local turn stream. Later enrichment does not rewrite already emitted files. `cost_usd` is native USD usage; `estimated_cost_usd` estimates the credit portion. They are not interchangeable and neither is a final invoice.

### COSTS: organization-scoped hourly data

`COSTS` uses the **organization** logs route and `API_PLATFORM_ORG`; it is not available from the workspace logs route. Its payload keys are `day`, `hour`, `organization_id`, `identity`, `product`, `surface`, `client`, `model`, `service_tier`, `reasoning`, `measures`.

`identity` can contain `user_id`, `email`, `name`, `groups[]` (`id`, `name`) and `agent` (`id`, `name`). `measures.usage` can contain `text_input_tokens`, `text_cached_input_tokens`, `text_output_tokens`, `audio_input_tokens`, `audio_cached_input_tokens`, `audio_output_tokens`, `image_input_tokens`, `image_cached_input_tokens`, `image_output_tokens`, or aggregate `text_total_tokens`, `audio_total_tokens`, `image_total_tokens`.

Each `measures.billing[]` entry has `sku`, `quantity` (`value`, `unit`), `cost` (`value`, `unit`), and optional `estimated_cost_usd` (`value`, `unit`). Preserve `CREDITS` versus `USD`. The estimate applies to credit-priced entries; native USD should not be converted again. Negative adjustments and zero values retain their original unit.

### App, authentication, security and agent records

`APP_LOG.app_type` values: `SERVICE`, `OPEN_API`, `MCP`, `FIRST_PARTY_ECOSYSTEM`, `UNKNOWN`. Request and response are separate observations; a response may never arrive. App-specific extra fields are not a stable universal schema. `APP_AUTH_LOG.app_id` can be null after unlink/removal.

`AUDIT_LOG.action_result`: `SUCCESS`, `BLOCKED`, `ERROR`. `action_privilege`: `ADMIN`, `STANDARD_USER`. Request metadata can include `client_ip`, `client_ip_details`, `client_user_agent`, `client_ja3`, `client_ja4`, `destination_hostname`. The full action-name catalog follows later.

Channel audit actions additionally include `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`, `AGENT_TASK_DELEGATED`, `CODE_ENVIRONMENT_ACCESSED`. Their shared correlation fields are `flow_id`, reserved `flow_binding`, and optional verified `requester_account_user_id`. Slack attribution uses `slack_team_id`, `slack_user_id`, `slack_channel_id`, `slack_event_id`; Teams attribution uses `microsoft_teams_tenant_id`, `microsoft_teams_team_id`, `microsoft_teams_channel_id`, `microsoft_teams_user_aad_object_id`, `microsoft_teams_event_id`. Completion adds `execution_backend`, `failure_reason`; delegation adds `delegated_task_id`, `delegation_request_id`, `delegation_status`, `delegated_workflow_id`; environment access adds `environment_type`, `environment_name`, `environment_access_id`, `environment_status`.

`CODEX_SECURITY_LOG` sub-events: `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_CREATED`, `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_UPDATED`, `SCAN_FINDING_UPDATED`, `PROPOSED_PATCH_PR_CREATED`. They carry scan configuration/finding IDs, sanitized field snapshots or changes, and a PR URL when available. They are product audit observations, not proof that a vulnerability is fixed.

Deleted-user inclusion differs between per-user and workspace aggregation. Preserve UTC date/window semantics and pagination. Missing token or cost coverage must not be converted to zero.

The unified scope is `enterprise.analytics.usage.read`; the Codex-specific analytics scope is `codex.enterprise.analytics.read`. They are not interchangeable. A normal model API project key is not a workspace Admin key. [Analytics overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/analytics-api).

Type: `string`.

Each row is an `AUDIT_LOG.action` identifier from the public schema, including old compatibility actions still documented. The action name says what operation was recorded; `action_result` establishes success/block/error. The last column retains native field and allowed-value tokens from the action description; it is not a list of universally required top-level keys. This does not authorize performing any action listed here. Some RBAC activity has moved to the API Platform audit surface; both contracts must be consulted during migration.

blocks.text:
### Metrics excluded from the built-in Statsig route

These names are explicitly filtered for that route. A configured custom OTLP exporter is not subject to this exact-name exclusion list. Their presence in source does not mean OpenAI receives them through the default metrics route.

`codex.api_request`, `codex.api_request.duration_ms`, `codex.conversation.turn.count`, `codex.responses_api_engine_iapi_ttft.duration_ms`, `codex.responses_api_engine_service_tbt.duration_ms`, `codex.responses_api_engine_service_ttft.duration_ms`, `codex.tool.call`, `codex.tool.call.duration_ms`, `codex.turn.cost_microusd`, `codex.turn.token_usage`, `exec_server_client_requests_total`.

[Source: Statsig filter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/config.rs).

### Public-documentation names not found in this release inventory

Retained here so they are not silently lost. Absence from the pinned source does not, by itself, establish a formal deprecation. In particular, the current implementation uses `codex.cloud_config_bundle.*` where the public prose lists `codex.cloud_requirements.*`.
